declarations.description:
The activity feed is Home's record of what happened in the catalog: who queried what, which
schemas changed, what was certified and which plugin runs updated assets. Items are grouped by
day under sentence-case label headings ("Today", "Yesterday", "Monday 26 October"), never
uppercase text, and separated by hairlines, never boxed as cards. Put it in an `mm-panel`.

When `pending` is above zero a "3 new events" button appears at the top inside a polite live
region, so screen readers hear about new activity without losing their place; it fires
`mm-show-new`. `has-more` adds a "Load more" button that fires `mm-load-more`; set `loading`
while more are on their way. With no items it shows `loading` placeholders, an `error` with a
retry, or the empty state.

Keyboard: interactive items form one tab stop. Up and Down move between them, Home and End jump to
the first and last, and Enter or Space opens the item (`mm-activate` on the item, usually to open
a blade). Links inside an item stay in the tab order. This follows the list navigation of
`mm-list` (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/practices/keyboard-interface/).
declarations.name: MmActivityFeed

declarations.description:
One event in an activity feed, written as a full sentence: the actor, a verb phrase and the
target ("Jane Doe certified customers_dim", "support-triage-agent queried orders_daily").
People, agents and teams are told apart by the avatar's icon (the robot for agents), with the
kind word given to screen readers only; there is no "AGENT" text tag. The target is a link in
ink with an underline on hover and focus, set in mono only when it is an MRN (`target-mono`). The
time is relative, in the text face with tabular figures, with the absolute UTC time in a tooltip.

A row has one primary line (the sentence, truncated, with the time as a quiet caption at the end)
and at most one quiet secondary line. The status pill appears only
when something needs attention (`denied`, `failed`); `allowed` and `succeeded` are the default and
render no pill (the word stays in the accessible name). The detail line, usually the first line
of the SQL, is a single truncated mono line (it is code) in `mm-text-2`; the full statement
belongs in the blade.

With `interactive`, the whole row is a button that fires `mm-activate`, usually to open a blade,
and the actor and target links stay separately clickable above it.

declarations.description:
Every tabbable element under `root`, in flat-tree order, through shadow roots and slots. Used to
keep Tab inside the open navigation drawer.

The app shell lays out a Marmot screen: an optional full-width system banner, the sidebar on the
start edge, the top bar, the scrolling main area with page gutters (`space-8`, or `space-4` under
720px) and an optional details blade on the end edge. The page is paper; the sidebar sits on
`mm-chrome` behind a hairline (paper on Light, sunken on Peat), so the chrome stays quieter than the data it frames.

The shell provides the landmarks: the top bar is wrapped in a `header`, the content in `main` and
the blade in a labelled `aside`; slot an `mm-sidebar-nav` (a `nav`) into `sidebar`. A "Skip to
content" link is the first thing Tab reaches.

⌘B (Ctrl+B elsewhere) collapses the sidebar to a 56px rail and back, and the shell passes the state
to the slotted sidebar as `collapsed`. Under 720px the sidebar becomes an off-canvas drawer, opened
by the menu button an `mm-top-bar` shows at that width (or `openDrawer()`): a modal dialog that
keeps Tab inside it, closes on Escape, the scrim or a link, and returns focus to the button.
declarations.name: MmAppShell

declarations.description:
Area charts show one quantity over time, such as assets catalogued per day, as a key line over
a flat 10% tint of the same colour, never a gradient. They carry the key series only: when you
need context series, use `mm-line-chart`. The fill runs down to zero, so the range-frame y axis
spans zero to the maximum, labelled at both ends, with at most three dotted gridlines and no box.
Estimated trailing points (`estimated`) are dashed and hatched instead of tinted, and
`annotations` take the same leader and dimension-bracket notes as the line chart.

Keyboard: Tab to the chart, then Left and Right move between points and show the tooltip;
Home and End jump to the ends; Escape hides the tooltip.

Burnt sienna is for links in prose. */ a.name { color: var(--mm-text); text-decoration: none; } a.name:hover, a.name:focus-visible { text-decoration: underline; text-decoration-thickness: 1px; text-underline-offset: 2px; } .caption { font: var(--text-caption); color: var(--mm-text-2); overflow-wrap: anywhere; margin: 0; } .muted { color: var(--mm-text-2); margin: 0; } dl { display: grid; grid-template-columns: max-content minmax(0, 1fr); gap: var(--space-1) var(--space-4); margin: 0; } dt { font: var(--text-label); letter-spacing: var(--tracking-label); color: var(--mm-text-2); padding-block-start: 1px; } dd { margin: 0; min-inline-size: 0; overflow-wrap: anywhere; } .num { font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .error { display: flex; gap: var(--space-2); align-items: flex-start; color: var(--mm-danger); margin: 0; } .error mm-icon { margin-block-start: 1px; } `
declarations.description: Shared card layout for the asset and person cards.

Asset cards summarise one catalog asset: its provider logo and name (an ink link with `href`,
underlined on hover and focus), a sentence-case caption of real metadata ("Table · 14 cols"),
the MRN as a quiet caption in the text face (mono is kept for the one MRN in the page header),
the description clamped to two lines, owners, tags (with `pii` and `certified` in their
own colours), the row count in tabular figures and when it was last updated. They are built for
`mm-hover-card` and also work on their own; set `framed` for a bordered surface when the card
is not already inside a panel or popover, since cards never nest in cards.

`loading` holds the shape with a skeleton (after the usual 200ms delay); `error` replaces the
content with the message, in crimson with an icon. An asset with no description says so rather
than leaving a gap.

declarations.description:
The query audit log records every query run through Marmot: who ran it (a person, or an agent and
the service account it runs as), from which client, against which source, what it asked, how many
rows came back and whether it was allowed. Rows are 36px and dense; the header band is sticky
inside the log's scroll area (set `--mm-audit-max-height` for long views).

It is an ARIA table, not a grid: the log is read-only data, so screen readers keep their table
commands (moving by row and column, hearing headers), and the only control per record is a
disclosure button. A grid would force cell-by-cell arrow keys onto people who only want to move
between records and open one. Each `mm-audit-row` is a row group holding its row and, when
expanded, a full-width detail row, like a `tbody` per record. Columns are shared through
`--mm-audit-columns`.

Keyboard: the log is one tab stop. Up and Down move between records, Home and End jump to the
first and last, Enter or Space expands or collapses the focused record, and Escape collapses it
from anywhere inside and returns focus to its row. Tab moves into an expanded record's actions.
Disclosure pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/

declarations.description:
One record in the query audit log. The row shows the time in UTC (text face, tabular figures), who
ran it (an agent by its robot avatar, never an "AGENT" tag), the client as a plain word (API, CLI,
MCP, never a coloured badge), the source with its provider logo, the rows returned (right-aligned
and tabular, with "Truncated" when the result was cut off) and the outcome. The statement is not
previewed in the row; it appears, in mono, only when the record is expanded. Don't badge the happy path: only
`denied` and `failed` show a status pill; an `allowed` record leaves the cell empty, with the
word for screen readers.

Expanded, it shows the full statement, highlighted as SQL on the code ground (the same highlighter
and edge as `mm-code-sample`), with a copy button in its own column, the decision ("Denied
because svc-support has no grant on shop.public.customers"), the duration, the tables read as
MRNs with copy buttons (mono, since people copy them), and "Open in editor" and "Run again".
declarations.name: MmAuditRow

slots.name: actions

declarations.description: The accessible name of an avatar: the name, with the kind word for agents and teams.

Avatars say who did something: a person, an agent or a team. People show their photo, or their
initials in ink on `mm-info-soft` when there is no photo or it fails to load. Agents always show
the `smart-toy` robot on `mm-primary-tint` instead of a photo, so an agent can't pass for a
person. Teams show the `groups` icon on `mm-sunken`. The tint is secondary: the icon or the
initials carry the difference, and the accessible name says "agent" or "team" too.

Avatars are the one round thing besides status and filter pills. Sizes are 20, 24 (default), 32
and 40px. The accessible name is `name` (with the kind word for agents and teams); set
`decorative` when the name is printed next to the avatar, as in `mm-owner-chip`.

declarations.description:
The system banner runs full width across the top of the app shell for messages that apply to
the whole instance, such as the server-configured banner in Marmot OSS or planned maintenance.
An icon, one sentence, an optional link and an optional dismiss button, on a soft status fill
or `mm-sunken`, closed by a hairline rule. No stripe. One banner at a time.

declarations.description:
Bar charts compare categories. Bars are grey with square tops; one bar can be highlighted in
the key colour (`highlight`), the only colour on the chart. Values are printed directly at the
bar ends in 13px mono; when bars are too narrow for every label, only the highlighted and
largest bars are labelled and a range-frame axis appears instead. Estimated or stale bars are
hatched, never recoloured.

`orientation="horizontal"` is the ranked-list form (failed runs per pipeline, queries per
agent), with the category names in a column and `sort="desc"` to rank them. Stacked bars take
`stack` (at most three names) and `values` per bar: the first two segments are greys and the
third is the key colour, labelled directly beside the last bar instead of in a legend.

Keyboard: Tab to the chart, then the arrow keys move between bars and show the tooltip; Home and
End jump to the ends; Escape hides the tooltip.

declarations.description:
Breadcrumbs show where a page sits: Discover › PostgreSQL › shop › public › orders. They are a
`nav` landmark named "Breadcrumbs" around an ordered list. Separators are chevrons hidden from
assistive technology and mirrored in right-to-left text. The last crumb is the current page: plain
ink text with `aria-current="page"`, not a link. Earlier crumbs are quiet `mm-text-2` links.

With more than `max` crumbs (default 4), or when they do not fit, the middle ones collapse into a
"…" menu button, keeping the first crumb and as many of the last as fit. Crumbs are always in the
text face, asset paths (provider, database, schema, table) included: breadcrumbs are never mono.

Pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/breadcrumb/

declarations.description:
A button group gathers related buttons under one label: view switches in a toolbar, zoom
controls on the lineage canvas. Spaced groups sit `space-2` apart; `attached` groups join the
buttons edge to edge with one shared border and square inner corners, and each button keeps its
own focus ring and tab stop. For one choice among options, use a segmented control instead.

https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/ covers arrow-key toolbars; a button group is a
plain `role="group"` and every button stays in the tab order.

declarations.description:
Callouts surface one message inside a page: a stale source, a truncated result, a failed run.
A soft status fill, a 16px status icon, a bold heading in ink written as a full sentence, and a
body in `mm-text-2` that says what to do. No coloured stripe and no border.

`compact` is the inline alert: one line, smaller padding, for forms and table toolbars.

Callouts are `role="status"`, so changes are announced politely. Set `urgent` only when the
message must interrupt (a query that was just denied), which makes it `role="alert"`. With
`dismissible`, the close button fires `mm-dismiss` and hides the callout unless the event is
cancelled. Escape inside the callout also dismisses it.

declarations.description:
The shared behaviour of every focusable Marmot chart. Not an element on its own.

The plot is one focusable `role="img"` region named by a summary sentence generated from the
data. Left and Right move a focus marker between data points and show the ink data tooltip;
Home and End jump to the ends; Escape hides it. Pointer hover does the same without moving
focus. A visually hidden table carries every value. The width follows the container through a
ResizeObserver; before the first measurement (and on the server) the chart draws at
`default-width` and scales to fit, so it renders without JavaScript measurement.

Plots are drawn left to right in every direction, as time and number lines are in Arabic and
Hebrew dashboards, so the arrow keys always follow the screen.

Checkboxes turn one option on or off: "Notify me when this pipeline fails", "Include
deprecated assets". The label sits beside the 16px box and is clickable, with an optional
description line under it. `indeterminate` shows a dash for a parent whose children are mixed.

The checked box is filled with ink (`mm-text`) and carries an `mm-on-inverse` tick. It is not
burnt sienna: the guidelines reserves burnt sienna for the primary action, links, the active tab and the
current selection, at most once per row. A settings list can hold a dozen ticked boxes, which
would spend the accent many times over and read as a row of selections. Ink keeps the state
unmistakable at 17:1 while leaving the accent for what it marks.

Keyboard: Space toggles (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/checkbox/). The control is a
native checkbox inside the shadow root, so it is announced as mixed when indeterminate.

Form-associated: submits `value` (default `on`) under `name` only while checked, as a native
checkbox does. `required` means it must be ticked. The `checked` attribute is the default the
form resets to.

declarations.description: Shared styles for the frame, fallback and footer, reused by `mm-sql-editor`.

The code editor is CodeMirror 6 on the warm near-black code ground, in Light and Peat alike:
Geist Mono at `mono-editor`, the `mm-syn-*` syntax colours, a line-number gutter
and `radius-md`. It edits SQL, JSON (role documents) and YAML (pipeline configs), or plain text.

CodeMirror is loaded with a dynamic import in `firstUpdated`, so the element costs almost nothing
until it is used. Until then, and during SSR, it renders a static highlighted copy of `value` with
the same metrics, so nothing moves when the editor arrives. Set `lazy="interaction"` to wait for
the first focus or pointer press before loading at all, for pages with many editors.

Tab indents. To leave the editor from the keyboard, press Escape and then Tab (CodeMirror's
tab-focus mode), which the editor announces in its description. When a completion list is open,
the first Escape closes it, so press Escape again before Tab. Code always runs left to right,
even in a right-to-left page.

Diagnostics (`diagnostics`) draw a wavy crimson underline, a gutter mark and a message under the
editor with the line and column, so an error never relies on colour alone.

The element is form-associated and submits `value` under `name`.
declarations.name: MmCodeEditor

declarations.description:
Code samples show read-only code in documentation and marketing: the warm near-black code ground
in both themes, Geist Mono at `mono-editor`, and a copy button that confirms with
"Copied". There are no window dots and no language badge; an optional `filename` sits above the
block in `mm-text-2`, outside the dark ground.

Highlighting is a small built-in tokenizer for SQL, shell, JSON, YAML, TypeScript and JavaScript,
HCL and Go. It runs in `render()`, so the sample is highlighted during SSR too. Give the code in
`code`, or as the element's text (indentation is removed). Long lines scroll, or wrap with `wrap`
(use it for logs in narrow places such as drawers). With a `filename`, Copy sits beside it so the
code keeps its full width; without one, Copy keeps its own column at the end of the block, so
code never runs under it.
Use `highlight="3,5-7"` to pick out lines. Code always reads left to right, even in RTL pages.

declarations.description: Styles for the text input inside a combobox box, shared with mm-multiselect.

Comboboxes let people type to find one value in a long or remote list: an asset, an owner, a
glossary term. Typing filters the list (list autocomplete, manual selection) and emphasises the
matched text. Options come from slotted `mm-option` elements or from an async `loader`, which is
debounced by 150ms, aborts stale requests, shows a loading row only after 200ms and offers a retry
when it fails. With `allow-custom`, free text is accepted as the value.

Keyboard follows the WAI-ARIA editable combobox with list autocomplete pattern
(https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/examples/combobox-autocomplete-list/): Down and
Up open and move, Alt+Down opens without moving, Enter selects, Escape closes and then clears,
Home and End move the caret.

declarations.name: fuzzyScore
declarations.description:
Scores `label` (and its keyword synonyms) against a query, case-insensitively. Every
whitespace-separated token must match. Per token, a prefix of the label scores highest, then the
start of a word, then any substring; keyword matches score below label matches. Returns null when
a token does not match.

The command palette is the keyboard entry point to everything in the catalog. It mixes page
navigation and actions (`commands`, filtered locally with a prefix, then word-start, then
substring scorer that also matches keyword synonyms) with live catalogue results (`search`,
debounced 120ms, stale calls aborted). It opens and closes instantly: the guidelines bans animated
command palettes, so the dialog has no transition at all.

Scope the search with Tab (All, Assets, Glossary, Teams, Pages) or the chips under the input, and
type `>` to see commands only. With an empty query it shows `recents`, then every command.

Every row shows its own shortcut as a keycap when it has one, and the active row also shows the
Enter keycap, so the key that will act is always on screen. Rows without a shortcut show only the
Enter keycap when active.

Built as a modal `<dialog>` containing an ARIA combobox (the input, with `aria-activedescendant`)
that controls a grouped listbox, following
https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/examples/combobox-autocomplete-list/. Keys:
ArrowDown and ArrowUp move and wrap, Home and End jump to the first and last result, PageDown and
PageUp move by ten, Enter opens the active row, Tab and Shift+Tab change scope, Escape closes and
returns focus to where it was. Set `global-shortcut` to toggle with ⌘K or Ctrl+K anywhere.

Selecting a row fires `mm-select`; unless that is cancelled, the palette then calls the command's
`run()` or navigates to its `href`. It always closes.

With `search-href` (such as `/discover?q={query}`), every typed query ends with a "Search the
catalog for …" row that opens the full search page, so people can always get from the palette to
every result, including when nothing matched. It fires `mm-search-all`; cancel it to route in a
single-page app.

Confirm dialogs stop a destructive or irreversible action until the person agrees to it. The
heading states the consequence as a question ("Delete orders_daily?"), the body says exactly what
is destroyed (lineage edges, owners, documentation) and what is not, and the confirm button is
crimson with an icon and a word naming what is destroyed ("Delete asset"), so it can never be
mistaken for the primary. Cancel is the secondary button and receives focus first, so Enter
never destroys anything by accident.

With `confirm-text`, a mono field labelled "Type orders_daily to confirm" appears and the confirm
button stays disabled until the field matches exactly (case and spaces included). Enter in the
field confirms once it matches. Use it for deletions that cannot be undone and reach other
people's work.

`tone="default"` uses the primary button for confirmations that are not destructive.

For one-off confirmations, `await MmConfirmDialog.confirm({ heading, body, confirmLabel,
confirmText })` creates the dialog, shows it, resolves `true` on confirm and `false` on cancel or
Escape, and removes it afterwards. Focus returns to the element that was focused when it opened.
It is announced as an `alertdialog`, named by the heading and described by the body.
Pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/alertdialog/

declarations.description:
The contour chart is Marmot's signature density view: query heat by hour and weekday, lineage
density or usage, drawn as isolines in `mm-contour` like a survey sheet. There are 4 to 6
bands; the heaviest is an index contour in `mm-contour-index`, labelled with its value the way a
map labels its index contours, so no legend is needed. Labelled points (`marks`) are annotated
with a leader line and a mono caption.

Give it either a `grid` of values (rows by columns, such as 7 weekdays by 24 hours, with
`x-labels` and `y-labels` for the range-frame axes) or `points` to estimate a density over
`x-domain` and `y-domain`.

Use it for summaries on Insights and reports. The contour motif is decoration elsewhere, and it
must never sit behind working data such as tables or forms.

Keyboard: Tab to the chart. In grid mode the arrow keys move a cross-hair between cells
(Left and Right through the columns, Up and Down through the rows) and show the tooltip; in
point mode Left and Right move between the marks. Home and End jump to the ends, and Escape
hides the tooltip.

Cron fields set a schedule, as on the pipeline schedule step. Pick a preset (Hourly, Daily at
02:00, Weekly on Monday) or choose Custom and type a five-field expression in mono. The helper
line says what the expression means in words ("Every day at 02:00 UTC"), syntax errors say
exactly what to fix, and the next five run times are listed in UTC so there is no doubt about when
a pipeline will run.

and select, Home and End jump to the ends, and Enter or Space on Custom moves focus to the
expression. In the expression, Enter commits the value.

declarations.description:
Data tables are the default way to show many records: schemas, members, audit logs, assets.
The header band is `mm-sunken` with 12px sentence-case `mm-text-2` labels and stays put while
you scroll. Rows are separated by hairlines, never zebra stripes; hover uses `mm-sunken` and
selected rows `mm-selected`, where tertiary text steps up to `mm-text-2`. Numbers are
right-aligned and tabular with units in the header; dates are relative, in the text face with
tabular figures; only types and IDs use mono cells. Links in cells are ink, underlined on hover
and focus. Status cells show a pill only when something needs attention: `succeeded` and
`allowed` are a plain quiet word. Rows follow
`--mm-row` (40px, or 36px under `data-density="compact"` or `density="compact"`): reduce row
height, never font size.

Rows are virtualised, so 100,000 records scroll smoothly while the markup stays an ARIA grid
with `aria-rowcount`, `aria-rowindex`, `aria-colcount` and `aria-colindex`.

Keyboard (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/grid/): the grid is one tab stop. Arrow keys
move between cells, Home and End go to the start and end of the row, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End to
the first and last cell, Page Up and Page Down move a screen at a time. On a header, Enter or
Space sorts, Alt+Shift+Left and Right move the column (`reorderable`), and F2 moves to the
resize handle, where Left and Right resize (Shift for bigger steps) and Escape returns. In the
body, Space toggles the row's selection (Shift+Space selects the range from the last toggled
row, as Shift+click does), Enter follows the row link or fires `mm-row-activate`, and on a
cell with buttons or links Enter (or F2) moves into it, Tab cycles its controls and Escape
returns to the cell. Ctrl+A (⌘A) selects every row.

Cells render inside the table's shadow root, so page stylesheets do not reach templates from a
column's `render`. Prefer elements (`mm-link`, `mm-text`, `mm-tag`, `mm-status-pill`), which
carry their own styles. The table also styles this set of classes inside cells, matching
`@marmotdata/css`: `mm-link` (ink in cells, underlined on hover and focus), `mm-code-inline` and
`code`, `mm-kbd`, `mm-dense`, `mm-label`, `mm-caption`, plus two cell helpers: `mm-mono` (mono
dense, for IDs and keys only) and `mm-muted` (`mm-text-3`, which steps up to `mm-text-2` in a selected
row). Number columns align their header with their values.

declarations.description: Resolves a value to concrete start and end instants. Relative presets end at `now`.

The date range picker sets the time window for run history, query audit and Insights. The trigger
reads as a sentence ("Last 7 days", or "12 Oct 2026, 09:00 to 27 Oct 2026, 17:30 UTC") with the
zone always shown. The popover holds relative presets on one side, which apply at once, and a
custom range on the other: a calendar grid, start and end times, then Apply or Cancel. The range is
marked with the selection tint, the endpoints with an ink fill and today with an underline, so
nothing relies on colour alone.

Keyboard follows the WAI-ARIA date picker dialog pattern
(https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/examples/datepicker-dialog/): arrows move
by day and week, Page Up and Page Down by month (with Shift, by year), Home and End to the start
and end of the week, Enter or Space picks the start and then the end. Arrow keys move through the
presets. Escape closes without applying. Tab cycles within the open popover.

Submits `${name}` with the preset key for relative ranges, or `${name}-start` and `${name}-end`
as ISO 8601 strings for absolute ranges.

A description list sets out an object's metadata as label and value pairs: the Details section
of the asset blade, a pipeline's configuration, a member's profile. Labels are the sentence-case
`label` style in `mm-text-2`; values are dense text that wraps anywhere, so long MRNs never push
the layout wider. Nothing is boxed: pairs are separated by spacing alone.

`layout="columns"` (default) puts a 120px label column beside the values. `stacked` puts each
label above its value, for narrow places. `inline-grid` lays pairs across 2 to 4 columns
(`columns`), for short KPI-like metadata such as rows, size and freshness.

The list is exposed as a list of term and definition pairs, since native `dl` semantics cannot
cross shadow roots.

declarations.description:
The details blade is the 36rem (`blade-w`) side panel on an asset page: plain sections separated
by hairlines on `mm-chrome`, with a hairline on its inline-start edge. It is never a stack of
cards. The head carries the title, an optional "Full view" link and a close button. Identifiers
such as MRNs wrap anywhere.

`mode="static"` (default) sits in the page grid as a labelled region. `mode="overlay"` slides
over the content from the inline-end edge with `shadow-float` (220ms, instant when opened or
closed from the keyboard, opacity only under reduced motion). It is a non-modal dialog: focus
moves to the close button when it opens and returns to where it was when it closes, and Escape
closes it.

With `resizable`, the inline-start edge is a handle: drag it, or focus it (a `role="separator"`
with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`) and use Left and Right to resize by
16px (flipped in right-to-left layouts) or Home and End for the minimum (320px) and maximum (half
the viewport). The width is remembered in `localStorage` under `storage-key`. With `collapsible`,
a button folds the blade to a 3rem rail, as the asset blade does.

Pattern for the handle: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/windowsplitter/

declarations.description:
Shared styles for the modal overlays. The scrim is flat ink from the theme (ink at 40% on Light,
paper at 60% on Peat, where paper is the darker end), never blurred.

Dialogs ask for one decision or one short task without leaving the page: a native modal
`<dialog>` on `mm-raised` with `radius-lg` and `shadow-dialog`, over a flat ink scrim (no blur).
The heading is a real heading in the 20px heading style and names the dialog; the optional
description is announced with it. Actions go in the `footer` slot with the primary last, after
Cancel. Long content scrolls inside the body while the header and footer stay put, gaining a
hairline once content runs under them.

Opening uses `showModal()`, so the page behind is inert and the dialog sits in the top layer.
Focus goes to the first `autofocus` element, otherwise the first control in the body or footer
(scroll areas such as a code sample or a log are skipped), otherwise the close button. Tab and Shift+Tab wrap inside the dialog. Escape, the close button
and (with `dismissible`) a click on the backdrop fire a cancelable `mm-request-close` first, so
a form with unsaved changes can keep the dialog open. Closing returns focus to the element that
opened it, and page scrolling is locked while it is open. It fades and rises over
`--mm-dur-dialog`, appears instantly when opened from the keyboard, and does not move under
reduced motion.

Any slotted element with a `data-close` attribute closes the dialog when clicked, with the
attribute's value as `returnValue` (`<mm-button slot="footer" data-close="cancel">`).
Pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/

declarations.name: diffColumns
declarations.description: Structured column changes between two versions, in the new version's order with removals where they were.

The diff viewer shows what changed between two versions of an asset. In `columns` mode it is a
table of schema changes: each row says what happened in a word with a glyph ("+ Added",
"− Removed", "± Type changed") and shows the before and after types in mono. Added rows carry a
faint moss tint and removed rows a faint crimson tint, always with the word, never colour alone.
Unchanged columns fold behind a "Show unchanged columns" button.

In `text` mode it is a unified line diff of two texts (DDL, YAML, a pipeline config) on
`mm-surface`, with old and new line numbers and + and − gutters; runs of unchanged lines beyond
`context` fold behind buttons that expand them in place. Long lines scroll sideways, or wrap with
`wrap`.

The header is a sentence-case caption of the comparison ("Schema version 41 → 42 · 3 changes")
with who or what made the change and when. Column names, types and diff lines stay mono.

The fold buttons are ordinary buttons with `aria-expanded`: Tab reaches them, and Enter or Space
toggles them.

declarations.description:
An accordion stacks related disclosures under one another, separated by hairlines: the sections
of a plugin's configuration or the FAQs on a docs page. With `single`, opening one closes the
others. Give each disclosure a `heading-level` that fits the page outline; the accordion sets
level 3 on any that have none.

Keyboard (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/accordion/): Tab moves through the headers and
any open content. Enter or Space toggles a header. Down and Up move to the next and previous
header, wrapping; Home and End move to the first and last.
declarations.name: MmAccordion

declarations.description:
Drawers are modal side sheets for work that needs more room than a dialog but should not leave
the page: connecting an agent or a source (CLI and API snippets), or a create form. They slide in
from the inline end by default (`placement="start"` or `"bottom"` for the others), on
`mm-raised` with `shadow-dialog` over the same flat ink scrim as a dialog. Widths are `sm`
(360px), `md` (`--blade-w`, 36rem, default) and `lg` (800px); `full` takes the viewport.

Behaviour is the dialog's: a native modal `<dialog>`, focus to the first `autofocus` element or
the first control, Tab wraps, Escape and the close button fire a cancelable `mm-request-close`,
focus returns to the opener and page scrolling is locked. The slide is a transform over
`--mm-dur-dialog` (220ms), instant when opened from the keyboard and still under reduced motion.
Placement follows the writing direction, so `end` is the left edge in right-to-left pages.
Pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/dialog-modal/
declarations.name: MmDrawer

declarations.description:
Empty states earn the one decoration Marmot allows: a topographic background field, never an icon
or an illustration. The field is an `mm-topography` sheet behind the text, cropped by the empty
state's box and dissolving towards its edges, in hairlines mixed from `--mm-rule` so the title and
sentence keep full contrast. There is no drawing above the heading: one title, one sentence and
one action. The title is the text-face `heading` style (the display face is kept for page titles);
the one sentence says what is missing and what to do ("Connect a plugin to catalogue this source.").
No mascot, sparkles or stock art, and at most one field per view.

Use `compact` inside panels: a `heading-sm` title and no field, so a page of panels never stacks
several.

declarations.description:
One group of filters in the Discover filter column: Type, Provider, Tags or Owner. The heading is
a disclosure button that collapses the group. Options are checkboxes with an optional icon or
provider logo and a mono, tabular count aligned to the end. Past `limit` options a "Show 8 more"
button reveals the rest (selected options always stay visible); past `filter-threshold` options an
inline field filters the list. "Clear" resets the group.

Checkboxes are native, drawn like `mm-checkbox` (ink fill, never burnt sienna), so Space toggles them
and Tab moves between them (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/checkbox/). The heading
button follows the disclosure pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/):
Enter or Space toggles, and `aria-expanded` reports the state.

declarations.description:
The Discover filter column: a "Filters" heading with "Clear all", a summary of applied filters as
removable pills, then one `mm-facet` per facet (Type, Provider, Tags, Owner). Facets are separated
by hairlines and spacing, never cards. Any change fires one `mm-filter-change` with every facet's
selection, ready to put in the URL or the search request.

The column is a labelled region. Removing an applied pill moves focus to the next pill, or to
the heading when none are left, so focus is never lost.

declarations.description:
Fieldsets group related controls under one legend: "Schedule", "Notifications", "Connection".
The legend uses the label style, an optional description sits under it, and controls stack
`space-4` apart (`space-2` for a list of checkboxes or switches). There is no box by default,
because structure should be felt and not seen; `bordered` adds a single hairline when a group
must stand apart inside a long form.

`disabled` disables every control inside, native and Marmot alike, and restores exactly the
controls it disabled when cleared. The legend and description name and describe the group for
assistive technology through a native fieldset in the shadow root.
declarations.name: MmFieldset

declarations.description: True when the file matches an `accept` list (extensions, exact MIME types, or `type/*`).

File drops take one or more files for upload, such as a dbt `manifest.json` or a CSV seed. A dashed
zone accepts dragged files and always offers a visible "browse" button that opens the native file
picker, so the control works fully from the keyboard. While files are dragged over it, the zone turns
sunken and its text changes, so the state never relies on colour alone.

Chosen files are listed with their name, their size in tabular figures and a remove button.
Files that are too large or of the wrong type are not added; a sentence names the file and the limit.
The element is form-associated: each file is appended to the form's FormData under `name`, `required`
blocks submission until a file is chosen, and form reset clears the list.

declarations.description:
Filter pills toggle facets in Discover and list views, such as a provider or a tag. They are round,
`mm-surface` with an `mm-rule` border that darkens on hover; a pressed pill is inverted ink. The
optional count sits in mono with tabular figures. With `removable`, the pill shows an applied filter
(“Provider: Snowflake”) with a remove button, for active-filter rows above results; move focus to
the next pill or the search field when you remove it.

Keyboard follows the WAI-ARIA toggle button pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/button/):
Enter and Space toggle.

declarations.description:
Shared field CSS for every Marmot form element: the label (12px, 600, sentence case, `mm-text-2`),
required and optional markers in words, help and error lines, and the 36px input box.

Classes: `.field` (label, control, messages stacked 6px apart), `.label` (`.marker` inside),
`.box` (the bordered input shell; add `.invalid`, `.disabled`, `.mono`), `.input` (a native
input or textarea inside `.box`), `.icon-btn` (24px ghost button inside `.box`), `.messages`,
`.help`, `.error` (crimson line with an icon), `.counter` and `.visually-hidden`.

`aria-invalid` inside the shadow root, and shows the browser's validation message inline (instead
of the native bubble) once the form has tried to submit.

A layout wrapper that gives any slotted control the Marmot field furniture: a label above, then
the control, then an error line and help text. Use it when composing a custom control; the
built-in controls (`mm-text-field`, `mm-select` and so on) render their own.

wired with `aria-labelledby` and `aria-describedby` instead. Attributes the author set are never
overwritten. Clicking the label focuses the control.

declarations.description:
Hover cards preview what a link points to (an asset, a person, an agent) without leaving the
page, so people scanning a lineage list or an audit log can check an owner or a row count in
place. Put `mm-asset-card` or `mm-person-card` inside, or any short read-only content.

The card appears 300ms after the pointer rests on the trigger or the trigger receives focus, not
instantly: moving the pointer across a dense table, or tabbing along a row of links, would
otherwise flash a card for every item passed over. It hides 150ms after both the pointer and
focus have left the trigger and the card, so the pointer can travel into the card. Touch input
doesn't open it. Escape hides it. It leaves focus where it is: the content follows the trigger
in the tab order while it is showing, and the trigger keeps its own name and destination, so the
card is never the only way to reach information. Shown from the keyboard, it appears without
a transition once the delay has passed.

Wrap the trigger (usually a link) in the `trigger` slot, or point `for` at its id.
declarations.name: MmHoverCard

declarations.description:
Line charts show change over time, grey first: context series in `mm-text-3`, and one key series
in burnt sienna (or slate with `tone="info"`), the only colour on the chart. Lines are labelled
directly at their ends in 13px mono, so there is no legend. The axes are range frames that span
only the data's minimum to maximum, labelled at their endpoints, with at most three dotted
gridlines and no chart box.

Annotate like a technical drawing: `annotations` takes points (a leader line with a dot
terminal and a mono caption, e.g. "Snowflake warehouse resize") and ranges (a dimension
bracket, e.g. an incident window). Set `estimated` to the number of trailing points that are
incomplete, such as the current hour: that tail is dashed and hatched, and marked "est.".

Keyboard: Tab to the chart, then Left and Right move between points and show the tooltip;
Home and End jump to the ends; Escape hides the tooltip. Pattern:
https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/ (focusable image with an active point).

declarations.description:
The lineage canvas draws how data moves between assets: HTML nodes on one transformed layer, SVG
edges beneath, on survey paper with a 16px dot grid that pans and zooms with the content. Layout
is dagre, left to right (mirrored in right-to-left documents), run in a worker for large graphs.
Pan and zoom use d3-zoom: drag, wheel and pinch. Embedded in a page that scrolls (a docs or
marketing page), set `modifier-zoom` so the wheel scrolls the page and zooms only with Ctrl or ⌘.

Edges never rely on colour alone: declared edges are solid ink-3, observed edges dashed moss,
mixed edges solid with a dashed overlay, and cycle edges dotted ochre ending in a "Returns to"
node rather than doubling back. Edge chips (origin and run count, or the job) appear on hover or
focus, or always with `show-edge-labels`. Agents that looked an asset up are grouped into one
agent cluster that expands. Nodes with neighbours beyond the depth show a "+3 upstream" handle.

Keyboard: the canvas is one tab stop (an `application` with `aria-activedescendant`). Right moves
downstream along an edge and Left upstream (flipped right to left), Up and Down move between assets
in the same column, Enter opens (`mm-node-activate`), Space selects, E steps through the focused
asset's edges (Delete removes one when `editable`), + and - zoom, 0 fits, F returns to the current
asset, and Escape leaves full screen. The minimap is a second tab stop: arrows pan, + and - zoom.

Performance: only nodes and edges in view plus a margin are rendered, panning moves one CSS
transform, and below 40% zoom nodes become plain shapes. 2,000 nodes pan at display rate.

Full screen is in-page (`fullscreen`); making it deep-linkable is the app's job, from
`mm-fullscreen-change`.

declarations.description:
The lineage legend explains every encoding on the lineage canvas, drawn exactly as the canvas
draws it: current, selected, stub, failed and cycle-return nodes, the agent cluster, declared,
observed, mixed and cycle edges with their dash patterns, and the edge chip. Edges never rely on
colour alone, so each sample shows its dash pattern as well.

Set `compact` for the canvas corner: a small "Legend" disclosure button that opens the same list
in a hairline panel. `open` reflects whether it is shown.

Keyboard (compact): Enter or Space on the button toggles; Escape closes and returns focus to it.
declarations.name: MmLineageLegend

declarations.description:
Estimated rendered height of a node, used by the canvas for layout without measuring thousands of
elements. Names wrap anywhere; 27 characters per 200px line is a safe estimate for 13px Geist.

Lineage nodes are compact cards on the lineage canvas: a sentence-case caption naming the asset
type ("Table", "Topic · stub"), the asset name (13px, 600, wrapping anywhere so long MRN-like names never overflow), and the provider
with its logo. Provider logos are the only colour; they are never recoloured.

States, each carried by shape or words as well as colour:
- `current`: the asset whose page you are on. 2px burnt sienna border on the burnt sienna tint. One per graph.
- `selected`: a 2px ink border and a tick at the end of the type strip. It is deliberately not the
  focus ring (a detached 2px ink outline with a 2px gap) and not burnt sienna, so current, selected and
  focused can all be told apart, alone or combined.
- `stub`: created by OpenLineage but not yet surveyed by a plugin. Dashed border on a transparent
  ground, "stub" in the type strip, and "Not catalogued yet" for assistive technology.
- `failed`: the last run failed. A crimson error icon and the words "Last run failed".

Variants: `cycle-return` closes a cycle without drawing an edge backwards ("Returns to orders_daily",
dotted ochre border, matching cycle edges). `agent-cluster` groups agents that looked up one asset
("4 agents looked this up") and expands to list them.

Standalone, set `interactive` to render the node as a button that fires `mm-node-activate`. Inside
`mm-lineage-canvas` the canvas owns focus and keyboard, so nodes are not tab stops there.
declarations.name: MmLineageNode

declarations.description:
Links take the reader somewhere: another asset, a run, the documentation. In running prose they
are burnt sienna with a 1px underline that thickens to 2px on hover. In lists, tables, rows and cards
use `quiet`: ink with no underline until hover or focus, so burnt sienna is left for the primary
button, the current tab and real links in text. Chrome links in toolbars and footers use `muted`
(ink-2). External links open in a new tab, carry an open-in-new icon and say so to screen readers,
in every variant. Focus shows the ink ring, never burnt sienna.

Follows the WAI-ARIA link pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/link/

declarations.description:
A list of records separated by hairlines: the body of a Needs attention or Pipelines panel, a
run history, the members of a team. Rows are `--mm-row` tall (40px, 36px in compact density or
with `dense`) and grow for a secondary line. Use a table when people need to compare columns.

When items are interactive (`href` or `interactive`), the list is one tab stop. Up and Down move
between interactive items, Home and End jump to the first and last, and Tab leaves the list.
Nothing is selected by moving: Enter follows the link or activates the item. This is listbox-like
navigation without selection, so the items stay links and buttons to assistive technology.

text, an optional secondary line in `mm-text-2` and an `end` slot for a status pill, a time

declarations.description:
The loading state is a survey being drawn: a patch of the abstract topography field, cropped and
dissolving at its edges, whose hairlines ink themselves in behind the caption. It appears after a
200ms delay so fast loads never flash, and then stays for at least 400ms. Under reduced motion the
lines appear at once. The field is background, never an icon: the caption (and its live
announcement) carries the meaning. For long operations, slot an `mm-progress` with a real count
("412 / 1,280 assets") rather than leaving people with an open-ended drawing.

Toggle `active` to finish loading rather than removing the element, so the 400ms minimum holds.
declarations.name: MmLoading

declarations.description:
A menu button opens a menu of secondary actions: the "More" button on an asset row or page
header. The trigger is an `mm-button` with `aria-haspopup="menu"` and `aria-expanded`; the menu
is a slotted `mm-menu`. Use an icon-only ghost button (`icon="more-horiz"` with `label`) for row
actions, or a labelled button with a chevron where the menu needs naming.

Keyboard (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/): Enter, Space and ArrowDown open
the menu and focus its first item; ArrowUp opens it on the last item. Escape closes it and returns
focus to the button.

declarations.description:
Menus hold secondary actions behind a "More" button or a right-click. A menu is a raised layer
with `radius-md` and `shadow-float`. Opened from the keyboard it appears instantly; opened with
the pointer it fades in over `--mm-dur-menu`. Destructive items come last, after a separator,
in crimson with an icon and a word naming what is destroyed ("Delete asset").

Without `anchor` the menu renders inline as a static list. With `anchor` (an element or the id of
one in the same root) it becomes a light-dismiss popover positioned against it, opened with `open`
or `show()`. Keyboard model: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/ (arrow keys
wrap, Home and End, typeahead, Enter and Space activate, Escape closes and returns focus to the
trigger, Tab closes).

declarations.description:
The metadata viewer shows the key and value metadata a plugin recorded for an asset: Snowflake
clustering keys and retention, dbt materialisation and dependencies, Kafka topic config. Top-level
keys read as a description list, keys in quiet mono (people copy them) and values beside them;
nested objects and lists of objects fold away behind a preview of their keys, and clicking anywhere
on such a row opens it. Every value uses the text face and ink: URLs as links (underlined on hover
and focus), ISO dates formatted with the raw value in a tooltip, numbers with tabular figures,
true and false as "Yes" and "No", null as "Not set". Lists of plain values read inline, comma
separated. Every row offers "Copy value" and "Copy path"
(e.g. `metadata.config.materialized`) on hover and focus. Search filters keys and values and
opens the path to each match. "View raw JSON" swaps the list for the pretty-printed JSON on the
code ground.

It is a tree (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/) with a roving tab stop: Down
and Up move, Right expands or moves to the first child, Left collapses or moves to the parent
(flipped in right-to-left), Home and End jump, Enter toggles a nested value or follows a link,
`*` expands siblings and typing a key name moves to it. Tab moves to the focused row's copy
buttons.

providers for a filter. Chosen values sit inside the field as removable tags (sunken, radius-sm,

then clears the text, Backspace in an empty field removes the last value. Left arrow from the
start of the field moves through the tags; Backspace or Delete removes the focused tag.

Notifications tell people what changed in the parts of the catalog they own or subscribe to: a
schema change on `shop.orders.v2`, a mention in a glossary comment, a finished plugin run, read
access about to expire. The same list fills the bell popover and the notifications page.

Unread notifications are marked three ways, never by colour alone: a small ink dot, a visually
hidden word "Unread" and a 600-weight title. With `filters`, an All, Unread and Read segmented
control filters the list in place. "Mark all as read" appears while anything is unread and fires
`mm-read-all`; unless that is cancelled, every item is marked read.

Keyboard: the notifications are one tab stop. Up and Down move between them, Home and End jump to
the first and last, and Enter opens one (`mm-activate`). The tab stop is the item's title link
(or button); from it, Tab reaches the target link and the "Mark as read" and "Delete" buttons. When an item is deleted, or marked read while the Unread filter
is on, focus moves to the next notification so keyboard users never lose their place.

the short message and the target link ("Two columns were added · shop.orders.v2"), truncated to a

declarations.description:
Number fields take a quantity: a retention period, a row limit, a timeout. Numbers are set in
tabular figures and right-aligned so they line up with the tables they configure. An optional
`unit` follows the number after a non-breaking space ("500 ms", "10,000 rows").

Keyboard follows the WAI-ARIA spinbutton pattern
(https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/spinbutton/): ArrowUp and ArrowDown change the value
by `step`, PageUp and PageDown by ten steps, Home and End jump to `min` and `max` when set. Steps
count from `step-base` (default 0), not from `min`, so `min="1" step="100"` gives 1, 100, 200 and
so on; `min` and `max` themselves are always valid. The
stepper buttons are labelled for assistive technology and stay out of the tab order, since the
arrow keys do the same job.

Form-associated: submits the number as text under `name`, validates `required`, `min`, `max` and
`step`, resets with the form and is disabled by a disabled fieldset.

declarations.description:
An owner chip names who owns or did something: a person, an agent or a team, as an avatar and a
name. Agents are shown by the robot avatar and teams by the group avatar, with the kind word
("Agent", "Team") given to screen readers only: there is no "AGENT" text tag. Agents may show the
service account they run as, after the name in a quiet caption. The difference is always an icon
(and, for assistive technology, a word), never the avatar tint alone.

By default it is plain inline content with no box: an owner appears in table cells, feed rows
and page headers, and a filled chip in every row would be chrome competing with the data
(structure felt, not seen). `radius-full` is reserved for avatars and pills, so when the owner
is being edited (`removable`), it becomes a `radius-sm` chip on `mm-sunken` like a tag, so the
remove button visibly belongs to it.

With `href`, the name is a link in ink with an underline on hover and focus, never burnt sienna:
links in rows, tables and cards are ink. With `hover-card` as well, people and agents get an
`mm-person-card` preview after 300ms. The remove button is named "Remove Jane Doe", fires
`mm-remove` on click, Enter, Space, Delete or Backspace, and never removes the chip itself: move
focus to a sensible neighbour when you remove it.

declarations.description:
The page header names the object or list a view is about. The title is the one display title in
the view (`display-title`), optionally led by a provider logo or an
icon. Under it sit, in order and only when given: a quiet sentence-case `caption` in the text face
and `mm-text-2` for facts shown nowhere else on the page ("1,284 rows · Updated 5 hours ago", a
hostname), leaving out the kind the breadcrumbs already give; the MRN
in mono with a copy button, the one place an MRN is set in mono; a one-sentence description;
then labelled rows for Owners, Tags and Links (places to go next, such as the source's own docs
or a runbook a rule added), each only when slotted. Actions sit at the end of the title row, with the primary last; when
there is no room beside the title they wrap onto their own row, aligned to the start under the
caption and MRN. Breadcrumbs or a back link go above.

Actions: one primary button and at most one secondary. A personal toggle such as Subscribe is an
icon-only ghost button with `pressed`, not a labelled secondary. Occasional and destructive
actions go into a "More" menu (`mm-menu-button` with icon `more-horiz` and the label "More
actions") as the first slotted action; places to go belong in the Links row, not in More. The header does not manage its actions, so this is yours to follow: slot at most three
things (More, secondary, primary).

Long identifiers such as `orders_daily_by_customer_region_rollup_v2` wrap anywhere rather than
widening the page. `compact` is for list pages and workspaces: the title (28px `display-section`,
still the page title), a count and the actions on one line, with the caption (if any) under the
title.

declarations.description: Page numbers to show: always the first and last, the current page with `siblings` either side, and ellipses for the gaps.

Pagination moves through long result sets: Discover results, the query audit log, run history.
It is a `nav` landmark labelled "Pagination" with previous and next buttons, page numbers with
ellipses, and a "Showing 1–50 of 1,284,019" readout in tabular figures. The current page carries
`aria-current="page"` and the selection tint with ink text. An optional page-size select offers
25, 50 and 100 rows; changing it keeps the first visible row on screen.

`variant="compact"` shows only previous, "Page 3 of 26" and next, for blades and narrow panels.
Leave `total` unset for cursor pagination, where the total is unknown: only previous and next
show, and `has-next` says whether there is another page.

Every control is a native button in the tab order (there is no composite keyboard model): Tab
moves through them and Enter or Space activates. Previous and next stay focusable when disabled
(`aria-disabled`), so focus is not lost on the first or last page.

declarations.description:
Panels group one subject on a page, such as Needs attention, Pipelines or Activity on Home. A
panel is `mm-surface` with a 1px `mm-rule` border and `radius-md`, and no shadow: the step from
paper to surface is enough. The head has an optional 16px `mm-text-3` icon, a 13px/650 title in a
real heading (text face, never display), an optional count and one right-aligned "View all" link
in ink, underlined on hover and focus.

The body is usually an `mm-list` or a table, edge to edge (`padding="none"`, the default). Use
`padding="default"` for prose or a form. Never put cards or other panels inside a panel: separate
its parts with hairlines or spacing. Nesting one panel in another warns in the console.

swaps the body for the `empty` slot, usually a compact `mm-empty-state`.

declarations.name: setExpanded
declarations.description: Sets aria-expanded on a trigger, through `expanded` on elements such as `mm-button` that render their own button.

Popovers hold a small piece of interactive content next to its trigger: a filter form, column
options, a share list. The panel is a raised layer (`mm-raised`, `radius-md`, `shadow-float`)
with square, simple edges and no arrow, positioned against the trigger and flipped to stay on
screen. It uses the native `popover="auto"` attribute, so it sits in the top layer, a click
outside closes it, and only one auto popover is open at a time.

Wrap the trigger in the `trigger` slot, or point `for` at the id of a trigger in the same
document or shadow root, or set `anchor` to an element. The trigger toggles the popover and
carries `aria-expanded`. Escape closes it and returns focus to the trigger; Tab moves through
the content in document order (place a `for` popover straight after its trigger) and leaving it
closes the popover. It is non-modal: focus stays on the trigger unless something inside has
`autofocus`. Give it a `label` to expose the panel as a named, non-modal dialog. It fades over
`--mm-dur-menu`, and appears instantly when opened from the keyboard.
Pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/

declarations.description:
The proportion bar replaces the donut. It is a single horizontal bar split into segments in
alternating greys, with one segment highlighted in the key colour, and each segment labelled
directly in 13px mono with its share, using leader lines when segments are too narrow for their
labels. Small segments (below `threshold` of the total) are grouped as "Other", so the bar never
needs a legend or a rainbow of categories.

(asset types next to their counts). The list shows grouped items individually.

Keyboard: Tab to the bar, then Left and Right move between segments and show the tooltip;
Home and End jump to the ends; Escape hides the tooltip.

declarations.description: Writes a tree as Marmot query syntax.

declarations.name: readQuery
declarations.description: Reads Marmot query syntax into a tree whose root is a group. Unknown pieces become free text, so nothing is dropped.

The query builder edits a search as groups of conditions, for anything the search bar's tokens
cannot say. Each group has an All, Any or None switch with a plain hint ("Every condition must
match"), and rows read as a sentence ("Where … and …", "or", "nor"); groups nest up to three
deep, indented with a rule, never boxed. A row is a field, an operator that
fits it and a value control that fits both. Operators follow what Marmot's query engine accepts
per field (see `operatorsFor`): a glossary term only "is" or "matches" a pattern, a provider has
no comparisons, metadata takes everything including "between" for numbers. Any metadata path can
be typed as the field, with suggestions from `loadFields`, and values suggest from `loadValues`.
Free text is a row too ("Any field contains orders"). It reads and writes the full query syntax, so
every query can be built here; nothing falls back to text.

Open it from the search bar ("Build query"). It edits a copy: Apply fires `mm-apply` with the
new query, Cancel or Escape fires `mm-cancel`. Every change fires `mm-input`, so the page can
set `count` to the live number of results. Adding and removing rows and groups is announced,
and focus moves to the new row or to the control that adds one.
declarations.name: MmQueryBuilder

declarations.name: tokenize
declarations.description:
Splits a Marmot search query into tokens covering every character, in order: free text,
quoted phrases, `field:value` pairs, `@metadata.path` keys, operators (`: = != < <= > >= !`),
`contains` and `range` after a field, `[a TO b]` ranges and the boolean keywords AND, OR and NOT.

The Discover search box. People type free text mixed with Marmot's search syntax
(`type:table`, `provider:snowflake`, `@metadata.owner = "Analytics Engineering"`, AND, OR, NOT),
and the structured parts are highlighted as they type: field keys in slate, values in ink,
operators and boolean keywords in ink-2. The field is a real `<input>` with transparent text under
an aria-hidden highlighted copy, so caret, selection, IME and screen readers behave natively. Every
token is set in the text face so the copy lines up with the caret to the pixel.

Pass `createQuerySuggest({ fields })` as `suggest` for editor-style completion: `@` lists the
fields, then operators, values and AND, OR or NOT follow as the query is typed.

Optional suggestions follow the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with a listbox popup
(https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/combobox/): ArrowDown opens and moves, ArrowUp moves,
Enter or Tab accepts the active suggestion, Escape closes. Enter with no active suggestion fires
`mm-search` and submits the owning form unless the event is cancelled. The `shortcut` key ("/" by
default) focuses the field from anywhere on the page.

declarations.description:
The results grid shows SQL output: often hundreds of columns and up to a million rows,
virtualised in both directions with fixed-size cells. Every cell is mono (`text-mono-dense`),
numbers are right-aligned and tabular, NULL is the word "NULL" in `mm-text-3`, booleans read
`true` and `false`, and long strings end in an ellipsis. The row number gutter and the header,
which gives each column's name and type on two lines, stay put while you scroll.

Select a cell, or a range with Shift and the arrow keys (or Shift+click, or a drag), and
Ctrl+C (⌘C) copies it as tab-separated values that paste into a spreadsheet. Enter or a
double-click opens the cell inspector with the full value, JSON pretty-printed, and a copy
button; Escape closes it. The status line states rows, columns and run time, and a truncated
result is marked with a warning icon and the word. A Table, CSV and JSON switch in the footer
shows the same result as text, with Copy and Download beside it; the text is built in the
browser, and cancelling `mm-export` skips the client-side download so the server can export.

Give `rows` as an array of arrays, or stream with `getRow(i)` and `rowCount`, calling
`refresh()` as rows arrive.

Keyboard (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/grid/): one tab stop. Arrow keys move,
Home and End go to the row's first and last column, Ctrl+Home and Ctrl+End to the first and
last cell, Page Up and Page Down move a screen. Shift with any of these extends the selection.
On a header, Enter or F2 moves to the resize handle, where Left and Right resize and Escape
returns.

declarations.description:
Run strips show the pass and fail history of a pipeline as small square cells, oldest first and
the newest at the end, as on Plugins and an asset's run history. Every status has a shape as well
as a colour: succeeded is a solid moss square, failed is crimson with an ×, partial is half
filled in ochre, skipped is an outline with a dash, queued is a dotted outline, and running is
slate with a centre dot that pulses only with `live` (never under reduced motion).

left), Home and End jump to the oldest and newest, and each run's id, status, start time and
duration show in the ink data tooltip and are announced. Enter or Space (or a click) fires
`mm-select`. Escape hides the tooltip. Pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/grid/

declarations.description: A small YAML writer for schema documents: maps, lists, strings, numbers, booleans and null.

The schema outline is the Schema tab of an asset, for flat SQL tables and deep Avro or JSON
schemas alike. Each field reads as two lines: its name, its type in everyday words ("Text",
"Money (GBP)", "List of line item", "One of 3 values: WEB, IOS, ANDROID") and markers (Key,
PII, Certified), then its description with glossary terms beside it. Only exceptions are
marked: "Optional" for a nullable field, "Edited" for a description a person changed, and the
filled share when a field has gaps. Groups fold into a tree only where nesting exists, with a
hairline guide per level; top-level groups start open. `density="compact"` shows one line per
field for wide tables.

Selecting a field opens a side panel with the exact type, its values (filled share, distinct
count, range, histogram, allowed values, default), who can see it, glossary terms and a copyable
path. A Structure, JSON and YAML switch shows the schema as text with a copy button, from
`source` (the original Avro or JSON Schema document) when given, or from `columns`.

It is an ARIA treegrid (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treegrid/) with row focus: one
tab stop; Down and Up move between rows, Home and End go to the first and last; Right expands a
group or moves to its first field, Left collapses it or moves to its parent (flipped in
right-to-left); Enter opens the field panel and Escape closes it, returning focus to the row.

declarations.description: Reads a query into the model, or null when it needs the text view (brackets across fields, OR between fields).

The search bar is the query builder. Free text and conditions live in one field: each condition
is a neutral token in plain words ("Type is Table", "Provider is Snowflake or BigQuery"), and
clicking a part of a token edits it (the field, the operator, or the value with a picker that
fits the field: a list of known values, a text box, or a from and to pair for ranges). Several
values of one field read as "is X or Y". There is no separate builder and no mode to switch.

Add a condition by typing `@` (editor-style completion walks field, operator, value), in the
query builder, or from outside, such as a facet sidebar setting
`value`. "Build query" opens `mm-query-builder` in place of the bar, for groups that match all,
any or none; Apply writes the result back. "Show as text" swaps the tokens for the raw query in
place; a query the tokens cannot show (groups, OR between fields) shows as text with Build query
beside it, never as a dead end.

Keyboard: Left at the start of the text moves into the tokens, Left and Right move between their
parts, Enter or Space opens a part's editor, Escape closes it and returns focus, Backspace on an
empty text box selects the last token and a second Backspace removes it, Delete removes the
focused token. Changes are announced politely. Enter in the text box fires `mm-search`.
declarations.name: MmSearchBar

rather than seen: a heading, an optional sentence of description and actions at the end of the

face, which is kept for the page title.

declarations.description:
The app's main navigation, on `mm-chrome` (paper on Light, sunken on Peat) down the start edge of the app shell. Destinations sit in
`mm-nav-group`s with sentence-case labels (Catalog, Work, Operate), with Settings and the Cloud
organisation switcher in the `footer` slot. The current page is the one place the navigation
carries colour: the burnt-sienna tint with ink text. Everything else is `mm-text-2` so the chrome stays
quieter than the page.

With `collapsed` the navigation becomes a 56px icon rail: labels become tooltips, group labels
become hairlines and counts become dots. Inside `mm-app-shell` the shell sets `collapsed` (⌘B), and
the toggle button at the foot asks the shell to switch.

Keyboard: items are links, so Tab moves through them in order (the APG disclosure navigation
pattern, https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/disclosure/examples/disclosure-navigation/).
As a shortcut, ArrowUp and ArrowDown also move between items and group headings, and Home and End
jump to the first and last. This is deliberately not a roving tabindex: every destination stays one
Tab away, as links in a landmark should.
declarations.name: MmSidebarNav

declarations.description:

lineage depth, a row limit, a sampling rate. The value is always printed beside the label in a mono,
tabular readout with its unit, so nobody has to guess from the thumb. The track is `mm-rule`, the
filled part `mm-text-2` (never burnt sienna) and the thumb is ink with the standard focus ring. With
`range`, two thumbs set a lower and upper bound. Use a number input when people know the exact value.

Keyboard follows the WAI-ARIA slider and multi-thumb slider patterns
(https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/slider/ and
https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/slider-multithumb/): arrows step (left and right flip in
right-to-left), Page Up and Page Down move a tenth of the range, Home and End go to the limits.

declarations.description:
Small multiples show per-source or per-domain health as a grid of small line or area charts on
one shared y scale, laid out like the sheets of a survey map: hairline sheet edges and the series
title above each plot. Plots in a grid row share one baseline, whatever their titles.
Every sheet's y axis is a range frame spanning only that sheet's own minimum to maximum on the
shared scale, so the extremes are labelled without repeating a full axis. Times are labelled
along the bottom row. Lines are grey; `highlight` draws one sheet in the key colour.

Each sheet is focusable: Left and Right move between its points and show the tooltip, Home and
End jump to the ends and Escape hides it. A visually hidden table carries every value.

declarations.description:
A split pane puts two related panes side by side (or one above the other) with a hairline
separator people can drag: the source tree beside the editor and results in Query, or the term
list beside the article in Glossary. The separator is a 1px `mm-rule` line with a wider grab
area; it darkens on hover, while dragging and on focus. Panes are never boxed: the hairline is
the only structure.

The size of the start pane is kept in pixels between `min-start` and the container size less
`min-end`. With `storage-key` it is remembered in `localStorage`. Double-clicking the separator
returns it to `default-position` and forgets the stored size.

Keyboard (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/windowsplitter/): the separator is a
focusable `role="separator"` with `aria-valuenow`, `aria-valuemin` and `aria-valuemax`. Left and
Right (or Up and Down when stacked) move it by 16px, flipped in right-to-left layouts so the
arrow always points the way the separator moves. Home and End move it to the minimum and maximum.
declarations.name: MmSplitPane

declarations.description: Changes that upper-case keywords and trim trailing whitespace, as offsets into the original text.

The SQL editor is the Query workspace's editor: `mm-code-editor` with the SQL grammar for the
source's `dialect`, autocomplete from catalog metadata, and the run and format keys.

- Ctrl+Enter (⌘+Enter on Apple) fires `mm-run` with the selection if there is one, otherwise the
  whole statement.
- Shift+Alt+F fires a cancelable `mm-format`; unless you cancel it, keywords are upper-cased and
  trailing spaces trimmed. Nothing else changes, so formatting never alters meaning.
- Completions come from `schema` (`{ 'shop.public.orders': ['order_id', …] }`) and from the async
  `completer`, whose results show their asset type and provider ("table · PostgreSQL") with the
  provider's logo. The popup sits on the code ground; Enter accepts, Escape closes.
- `error` puts the server's error inline at its line and column, with a status line under the editor.

Dialects: `postgresql` (default), `mysql`, `sqlite` and `standard`. Trino maps to standard SQL,
Snowflake, Redshift and DuckDB to PostgreSQL, BigQuery and ClickHouse to MySQL.
declarations.name: MmSqlEditor

declarations.description:
The default, happy-path states. Rows (activity, audit, notifications) render no pill for these:
a run that succeeded or a request that was allowed is what people expect, so it is not badged.

declarations.name: isHappyPath
declarations.description: True for a state that needs no pill in a row, such as `succeeded` or `allowed`.

Status pills state the condition of a run, asset or request in a word: a soft status fill,
status-coloured text and the word, with an optional leading icon or 6px dot. Colour is never
the only signal, and burnt sienna is never a status colour.

Set `state` for the common Marmot states (`succeeded`, `partial`, `failed`, `running`, `queued`, `stale`,
`denied`, `allowed`, `cancelled`, `skipped`), which picks the tone, glyph and default word for
you. `partial` is a run that finished with some failures: ochre (warning) with a part-filled ring,
kept apart from burnt sienna and the failed crimson. Set `status` directly for anything else and slot your own word.

Don't badge the happy path. Show a pill only when something needs attention (Denied, Failed,
Partial, Stale, Expiring, Running). "Allowed", "Succeeded", "Active" and similar are the default
and get no pill in rows, lists and tables: leave the cell empty, or give screen readers the word
as visually hidden text. `isHappyPath(state)` and `HAPPY_PATH_STATES` from this module tell you
which states to skip. A pill for a happy state is fine where the state is the subject, such as a
run's own page header.
declarations.name: MmStatusPill

declarations.description:
Steppers show where someone is in a multi-step flow, such as creating a pipeline (Choose plugin,
Basic info, Configure, Schedule and filters) or an asset. It is an ordered list: each step has its
number (tabular figures), a label and an optional description. Completed steps show an ink check, the
current step has `aria-current="step"`, ink text and the burnt-sienna marker (the one place a
stepper spends the accent, as the current selection), upcoming steps are muted, and a step with
`error` shows a crimson glyph with the words "Has errors". Every state is also given as a word to
assistive technology.

With `navigable`, completed steps become buttons (or links, with `href`) so people can go back;
the current and upcoming steps never are, because the flow validates each step before the next.
Tab moves between them and Enter or Space activates. Activating one fires `mm-step-change` and
makes it current unless the event is cancelled.

`orientation="vertical"` stacks the steps with the connector running down the markers, for side
panels and narrow dialogs.

declarations.description:
Tabs switch between views of one object, such as an asset's documentation, metadata, schema,
lineage and run history. Labels are 13px with a 16px icon, `mm-text-2` when inactive; the active
tab is ink with a 2px burnt-sienna underline inset from its edges. Counts sit in mono, muted and
tabular. Switching is instant: there is no sliding indicator.

Keyboard follows the WAI-ARIA tabs pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tabs/): the
strip is one tab stop; Left and Right move between tabs (flipped in right-to-left), Home and End go
to the first and last. With `activation="auto"` (default) moving focus selects the tab. With
`activation="manual"` focus moves without selecting, and Enter or Space selects: use it for heavy
panels such as lineage, so arrowing past them does not render them.

Overflow: when there are more than `max-visible` tabs (default 6), or the tabs do not fit the
width, the rest move into a "More" menu button at the end of the strip. Choosing one selects it
and swaps it into the strip, so the selected tab is always visible. The More button is its own tab
stop after the tablist, outside the tablist so the tablist only contains tabs.

Link tabs: give each `mm-tab` an `href` for URL-driven tabs (for example `/assets/orders_daily/schema`).
The strip then renders as a `nav` of links with `aria-current="page"` on the selected one, not as an
ARIA tablist. This is a deliberate trade-off: link tabs are navigation. Each link is a tab stop,
arrow keys do nothing, the page changes on activation, and screen readers announce links rather
than "tab 3 of 9". Use them when each view needs its own URL; use ARIA tabs for in-page views.
Set `value` from the current route so the right link is marked.
declarations.name: MmTabs

declarations.description:
Tags label an asset with a domain, classification or origin. They are plain by default: a
compact chip on `mm-sunken` in `mm-text-2`. Colour appears only when the tag means something:
`pii` (crimson, with a lock) and `certified` (moss, with a verified mark). `generated` and
`plugin` mark content generated by a plugin or an agent as a small outlined sentence-case caption
("Generated"), with no sparkle.

Long tags truncate with an ellipsis; the full text stays in the accessibility tree and is offered
as a native `title` only when it is actually cut off. With `removable`, the tag gets a remove
button named "Remove <tag>" that fires `mm-remove` on click, Enter, Space, Delete or Backspace;
the tag does not remove itself, so move focus to a sensible neighbour when you remove it. With
`href`, the tag text is a link.

declarations.description:
Interface text set in one of the token type styles. `body` (15px) is for prose, `dense` (13px) for
tables, sidebars, metadata and toolbars, `caption` (12px) for supporting text, `label` (12px, 600,
ink-2, sentence case) for field labels and column headers, and `mono` or `mono-dense` for machine
strings only: identifiers, MRNs, SQL, types, timestamps and keys. Never use mono as decoration.

`tone` changes the colour. Status tones (`danger`, `success`, `warning`) must sit beside a word or
icon that says the same thing, never colour alone. On raised layers (menus, popovers, dialogs) and
inside selected rows, use `secondary` rather than `tertiary` for captions, so they stay readable in Peat.

The element is inline by default; set `block` for a paragraph, which also caps prose at a 75-character measure.

declarations.description:
A heading with the right level for the document outline and the right type style for its role.
`level` (1 to 6) sets the semantics; `variant` sets the look, so a panel title can be an `h3` without
looking like one. Without a variant, level 1 is `display-title`, 2 is `heading`, 3 is `heading-sm` and
4 to 6 are `panel-title`.

The display styles (Geist at 600) are only for the page title (`display-title`, 34px, or
`display-section`, 26px, in a compact page header) and marketing heroes (`display-hero`, 56px), never
below 24px. Section, panel and empty-state headings use `heading`, `heading-sm` or `panel-title`. If a display
heading is styled smaller than 24px, it falls back to `heading` and warns in the console. One display
title per view region. Display numbers use tabular figures. Headings are sentence case.
