declarations.description:
A timeline lists what happened to one thing, in order: the steps of an access approval, the runs
of a pipeline, the phases of a single run. A 1px `mm-rule` spine joins small node markers whose
shape encodes the state, so colour is never the only signal: a filled circle is done, a ring is
pending, a ring with a centre dot is in progress and a cross is failed, and each step also carries
its state as a word.

`orientation="horizontal"` is the compact form for a run's phases (Queued, Started, Extracting,
Writing, Finished): one straight line through the markers, each step's name and time under its
marker, and the time between steps as a quiet caption on the line between them. The line is
darker up to the last finished step.

It is a list, not a widget: there is no keyboard model beyond any links or buttons inside steps.
In a narrow container the horizontal form wraps onto further rows rather than scrolling.

pipeline finishing. It sits on `mm-raised` with `shadow-float`: a status icon, one sentence, an
optional action and a close button. Toasts dismiss themselves after 5 seconds; the timer pauses
while the pointer is over the toast or focus is inside it. Danger toasts stay until dismissed.
Escape closes the focused toast.

Put toasts in an `mm-toaster`, or call `toast({ message })`, which uses one document-level
toaster. The toaster announces each message (politely, or assertively for danger), so the toast
itself carries no live region.

declarations.description:
Toolbars group the controls that act on one surface, such as the query editor's source select,
"Read only" status, row limit and Run query. They are chrome, so they stay quieter than the content
they frame: no fill, no border, controls separated by `space-2` and hairline separators.

Keyboard follows the WAI-ARIA toolbar pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/toolbar/):
the toolbar is one tab stop; Left and Right (Up and Down when vertical) move between controls,
flipped in right-to-left, and Home and End go to the first and last. Focus returns to the last
control used. Controls that use arrow keys themselves keep them: text fields keep Left, Right, Home
and End for the caret, an `mm-select` opens on Home and End, and an `mm-segmented-control` moves
its own selection with arrows, so place a segmented control at either end of a toolbar where you
can. Disabled controls are skipped.

Put controls in the default slot (start) and the `end` slot; the gap between them flexes.
`dense` sets 30px controls through `--mm-control`. `label` is required: it names the toolbar.

declarations.description:
Tooltips are square-cornered and ink-filled, in caption type, and appear instantly with no
delay or animation. They hide on Escape, when the pointer leaves and when focus moves away.
Keep them to a short phrase that adds to the trigger's name; never put actions or essential
information in one. `variant="data"` is the chart tooltip: mono key and value pairs with
tabular numbers, driven by `items`.

Attach with `for` (the id of a trigger in the same document or shadow root; the tooltip's text
is its content and the trigger gets `aria-describedby`), or wrap a single trigger and give the
text in `content` (the trigger gets `aria-description`, since a description cannot reach into
a shadow root). Pattern: https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/tooltip/

declarations.description:
The top bar runs across the main column of the app shell: 52px on paper with a hairline below. It
holds page context on the start side (breadcrumbs), the global search trigger in the centre, and
notifications, help and the avatar menu on the end side. It is chrome, so it stays quiet: no fills,
no burnt sienna, `mm-text-2` icons.

The search trigger looks like a search field, reads "Search the catalog" and shows the ⌘K keycap.
It does not take text: it fires `mm-open-search` so the app can open its command palette. With
`global-shortcut`, ⌘K (Ctrl+K elsewhere) fires it from anywhere on the page.

Inside `mm-app-shell` under 720px a menu button appears at the start to open the navigation drawer.

The avatar menu at the end of the top bar. The avatar is a person, so it is the person's initials
on `mm-info-soft` (or their picture) in a full circle. It opens an `mm-menu` with Account, the theme
(Light, Peat or System, so the toggle is no longer buried in the profile page), Language and Sign
out.

Choosing a theme sets `data-theme` on the document element (System removes it so
`prefers-color-scheme` applies) and fires `mm-theme-change`; cancel it to apply the theme yourself.
Account, Language and Sign out fire `mm-select` from the menu with the values `account`,
`language` and `sign-out`.

Keyboard (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/menu-button/): Enter, Space and ArrowDown open
the menu on the first item, ArrowUp on the last; Escape closes it and returns focus to the avatar.

declarations.description:
Topography is a background field, never an icon or an illustration. It is an unbounded survey
sheet: hairline isolines that run off every edge, cropped by the box they sit in, with no closed
island, frame, tile or plate. The lines are mixed from `--mm-rule`, every fifth (index) line only a
touch stronger, so text over the field keeps its full contrast in Light and Peat. Use at most one
per view, behind a moment that has room for it: an empty or error state, sign-in, a marketing hero
or closing band.

The element is absolutely positioned to fill its containing block and sits at `z-index: -1`, so
give the container `position: relative; isolation: isolate` and put the field first. It is
decorative (`aria-hidden`, `pointer-events: none`) and deterministic from `seed`, so it
server-renders the standard sheet. In the browser it watches its own aspect: a box wider than the
sheet (an ultrawide hero) gets a wider sheet with the same line spacing rather than a stretched
one, and lines stay hairlines at any size. For a zero-JS page use the `.mm-topography` class
from `@marmotdata/css`, which draws one fixed sheet.

declarations.description:
Trees show nested things one level at a time: the query source browser (source, database,
schema, table, column), a dbt project, folders of dashboards. Rows are dense (32px, 28px in
compact density), with a chevron, a provider logo or icon, the label, quiet secondary text (a row
count in tabular figures, or a column type in mono with `secondaryMono`), optional tags, and
actions that appear on hover and focus.

Nodes may be static (`children`) or loaded on expand: give a node `hasChildren` and set
`loadChildren(node, signal)` on the tree. A "Loading" row appears only if loading takes longer
than 200ms; a failure shows an error row that retries on Enter, Space or click. With
`filterable`, a filter field above the tree highlights matching labels and expands their
ancestors (among loaded nodes).

Only visible rows are rendered (`@lit-labs/virtualizer`), so 50,000 nodes stay fast. The tree
grows with its content up to `--mm-tree-height` and then scrolls.

Keyboard follows the WAI-ARIA tree view pattern (https://www.w3.org/WAI/ARIA/apg/patterns/treeview/):
focus stays on the tree and the active row is `aria-activedescendant`. Down and Up move; Right
expands, or moves to the first child; Left collapses, or moves to the parent (both flipped in
right-to-left); Home and End go to the first and last row; Enter activates (`mm-activate`);
Space selects (`mm-select`; with `selection="multiple"` it toggles); `*` expands every sibling;
typing a few letters moves to the next row starting with them. Tab moves to the active row's
actions, then out of the tree. Clicking a row selects it, clicking the chevron toggles it, and
double-clicking activates it.
